Marisa: Quick heads-up: spotted a weird quality regression during rw-3b int4 bring-up on long legal documents (~12k tokens). After ~5k tokens the model output becomes very high-entropy and generic — looks like phase/rotary alignment loss or a KV-cache wrap. Repro steps + small logs below.

Marisa: Repro command I used:
```
./repro --model=rw-3b-int4v2 --input long_legal.txt --seed 42 --max-tokens 12000 --report-kv=true
```

Marisa: Short excerpt from the run (tokens near 5120):
```
[5108] token=... entropy=3.1 text=...
[5119] token=... entropy=3.0 text=continues specific legal phrasing...
[5120] token=... entropy=7.2 text=and then something unrelated, generic filler...
KV_LOG: shard0 idx=5120 expected_idx=5120 got_offset=0x7f8a mismatch_flag=1
```

Jordan: which quant backend? int4 dynamic or int4v2 static? does this happen with int8/fp16 too?

Marisa: int4v2 dynamic quant. I tried fp16 and int8 on the same model + prompt — both look fine. This is only on int4v2 so far.

Tomas: I can repro locally on a 3090 with int4v2. Confirmed: disabling KV caching removes the symptom. Reproducer shows checksum diverge at the same index. Quick kv-check output:
```
KV_CHECKSUM: ok until idx=5119
KV_CHECKSUM: mismatch at idx=5120 (expected=0x1a2b got=0x3c4d)
rotary_phase_scale: pre=0.9996 post=0.5003 (scale dropped after shrink)
```

Lina: hypothesis: quantized matmul or pack/unpack around the KV write path is clamping/rescaling rotary angles when sequence position gets large (phase saturation). The scale drop looks suspicious — maybe an FP->INT rounding bug that only surfaces when pos_index > 4096 (or a wrap boundary).

Lina: quick patch to try (non-production, just for repro):
```
# in rotary kernel, apply small bias to preserve monotonic angle growth
phase = base_theta * (pos - pos_offset)
phase *= (1.0 + (pos / 1e5) * phase_scale_bias)
```

Marisa: I'll land a debug-build with that bias and run the full 12k job tonight on a dedicated test pool. @tomas can you start a binary bisect tomorrow to see whether this came in with the int4v2 codegen or an earlier runtime change?

Tomas: Yep. Bisect plan: test kernel-only branches first (old int4 kernels vs new), then check quantization preproc. If kernel is root, I'll tag eng-runtime and open a perf/regress bug.

Marisa: One odd detail — the drop is almost exactly at 5120 in many runs. Could be shard boundary or tile size. Also tried larger batch sizes and different batch alignment — same token index.

qa-robot: Queued long-context regression job: rw-3b-int4v2 12k tokens, with and without Lina's bias patch. job id: job-88234. Will post results when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sre-bot: FYI spun up a low-priority dedicated pool for these long runs to avoid tenant interference.

Jordan: if KV_CACHE_OFF removes it, maybe we add a short-term mitigation: detect checksum mismatch and fallback to un-cached path for affected requests until fix. Lower perf but avoids customer hits. Thoughts?

Lina: that's reasonable as a stop-gap. Add a metric/alert on KV_CHECKSUM mismatch frequency (<1/hr ok, >0.1% requests -> rollback).

Marisa: action items:
- @tomas: bisect kernel vs quantifier (owner)
- @marisa: run full repro with bias patch tonight, attach logs
- @jordan: add a longctx unit in the regression harness to catch this (test with 5k/10k/12k)
- @lina: prepare a minimal patch for CI to test impact on perf/accuracy
- @qa-robot: post results for job-88234 here when complete

Marisa: tagging priority P1 for onboarding impact (this blocks int4v2 rollout for long-context customers). Will follow up in the morning with logs from the debug run. :eyes:
